skills.definition: Programming in an explicitly named language. One language supports this core, not proficiency in other languages.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit language knowledge or personally implementing program logic in a named language.
skills.not_sufficient: A job title, degree, or teammate's implementation alone.

skills.definition: Algorithms or data structures, with actual knowledge or application stated.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit algorithm/data-structure knowledge, or personally implementing/analyzing described processing steps, structure operations/invariants, or computational complexity.
skills.not_sufficient: Using/comparing an existing component, generating records, or testing system behavior without describing that algorithmic mechanism. Accept relevant courses as knowledge, not inferred practice.
skills.practice_target: A specified algorithm/data structure whose steps, operations, invariant, correctness or complexity are described, not merely a symptom or system feature.
skills.practice_action: The applicant designs, implements or analyzes that described mechanism; using components or reproducing system behavior alone is insufficient.

skills.definition: Object-oriented design/programming or explicit software design patterns.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit OO knowledge, or describing class responsibilities, encapsulation, interface-based substitution, polymorphic behavior, object collaboration, or a design pattern.
skills.not_sufficient: Using an OO-capable language, writing an endpoint/handler, or using a framework alone. Do not infer an OO design from Java/C#/Python.

skills.definition: Using AI for coding or software development; unrelated AI tasks are insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Using an AI assistant specifically to write, inspect, test, or improve software.
skills.not_sufficient: AI image generation/moderation, general LLM use, or unrelated model evaluation.

skills.definition: Designing software components, their interfaces, or system architecture; implementation alone is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit system-design knowledge or explaining component boundaries, interfaces, data/control flow, architecture decisions or tradeoffs.
skills.not_sufficient: Implementing a feature or publishing API documentation without describing interface/architecture design.

skills.definition: Implementing backend services or APIs; consuming an API alone does not establish backend development.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit backend/API knowledge or implementing server-side behavior, routes, request handling, or API contracts.
skills.not_sufficient: Only consuming someone else's API or calling an SDK.

skills.definition: Implementing user interfaces or frontend applications; producing static analytical charts alone is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit frontend knowledge or implementing a user interface, client behavior, or accessibility.
skills.not_sufficient: Handing an API to a frontend teammate, producing static charts, or claiming the team's frontend work.

skills.definition: Distributed systems, microservices, event-driven architectures, or multi-tenant architectures; a single local service alone is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit distributed-system knowledge or describing coordination, service messaging, distributed state, microservice interactions or multi-tenant architecture.
skills.not_sufficient: A generic component or policy comparison without an explicit cross-boundary mechanism. Do not infer topology or coordination from a tool or domain.
skills.practice_target: Explicitly separate services/processes/nodes or isolated tenants, with an identified interaction, shared-state or isolation boundary.
skills.practice_action: The applicant designs, implements or diagnoses communication, coordination, replication, partitioning, consistency or tenant isolation across that boundary.

skills.definition: SQL queries or relational database work; generic structured JSON is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit SQL/relational knowledge or querying, designing, migrating, or operating relational data.
skills.not_sufficient: Structured JSON outputs or an unspecified database alone.

skills.definition: Non-relational data stores or search systems; name the actual supported technology.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit non-relational/search knowledge or using a named non-relational store/search mechanism for a described purpose.
skills.not_sufficient: Generic database work, local text matching, or SQL alone.

skills.definition: Concrete practices for maintainable, clear software; code quality does not automatically establish tests or reviews.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit maintainability practices such as refactoring, modularity, clear contracts, meaningful tests, or reducing code complexity.
skills.not_sufficient: Merely saying code was written or the system worked; do not infer separate code-review practice.

skills.definition: Software testing practices, test implementation, or executing software tests; unrelated model evaluation is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit software-test knowledge or designing, implementing, or executing tests of software behavior.
skills.not_sufficient: Unrelated model-quality evaluation or simply running the application.

skills.definition: Debugging or diagnosing software faults.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit debugging knowledge or diagnosing, tracing, reproducing, isolating, or correcting a software fault.
skills.not_sufficient: Merely viewing failed CI runs or monitoring a status indicator without diagnostic work.

skills.definition: Reviewing source code or explicit participation in code review; document review is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit source-code/PR review, examination of a proposed implementation, or actionable code-review feedback.
skills.not_sufficient: Reviewing CI status, reading logs, approving documents, or merging alone.

skills.definition: Git or another explicit source/version-control practice.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit source-control knowledge or personally working with commits, branches, diffs, merges, or PRs.
skills.not_sufficient: A GitHub link or configuring CI alone without a source-control claim/action.

skills.definition: Cloud platforms or services; record the actual provider, without inferring other providers.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit cloud knowledge or using an identified cloud platform/service for a described activity.
skills.not_sufficient: Docker, local deployment, or remote collaboration alone; do not infer cloud providers.

skills.definition: Containerization or orchestration; Docker evidence does not establish Kubernetes experience.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit container/orchestration knowledge or building, configuring, or running containers or workloads.
skills.not_sufficient: CI use or deployment alone; Docker does not establish Kubernetes.

skills.skill_name: 构建、交付与基础设施自动化
skills.definition: Build, delivery, infrastructure-as-code, or configuration automation; ordinary use of Git alone is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit build/delivery/IaC knowledge or automating builds, tests, releases, provisioning, or configuration.
skills.not_sufficient: Merely using Git, writing a script unrelated to delivery, or claiming another person's pipeline.

skills.definition: Explicit performance analysis or optimization of software/systems.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit performance knowledge or measuring/optimizing latency, throughput, resource cost, query performance, or comparable performance properties.
skills.not_sufficient: An unexplained improvement percentage or a product-success metric unrelated to performance.

skills.definition: Monitoring, telemetry, or operating software systems; ordinary written progress reports are insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit operational knowledge or implementing/using telemetry, monitoring, alerts, incident response, or maintenance of running systems.
skills.not_sufficient: Ordinary progress reports, handover documents, or one-off local tests alone.

skills.definition: Engineering reliability or scalability, supported by explicit relevant actions or knowledge.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit reliability/scalability knowledge or actions handling failures, correctness under load, recovery, redundancy, or scaling.
skills.not_sufficient: Simply deploying software or saying it is robust/scalable without relevant knowledge or actions.

skills.definition: Software security, authentication, authorization, or access controls; general safety moderation is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit software-security knowledge or implementing/testing authentication, authorization, access control, secure protocols, or vulnerability controls.
skills.not_sufficient: Content moderation, ordinary data validation, or database use alone.

skills.definition: SQL queries or relational data access; structured JSON alone is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit SQL/relational knowledge or SQL querying, relational joins, aggregations, or relational modeling/access.
skills.not_sufficient: Structured JSON, generic data handling, or a degree alone.

skills.definition: Programming or scripting specifically used for data analysis.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit analytical-language knowledge or coding data transformations, analysis, or analytical automation.
skills.not_sufficient: General programming unrelated to analysis or a teammate's script.

skills.definition: Spreadsheet-based analysis or explicit spreadsheet proficiency; ordinary documents are insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit spreadsheet proficiency or spreadsheet formulas, pivots, analysis, or workflow development.
skills.not_sufficient: Ordinary documents, a static table, or a spreadsheet file merely being present.

skills.definition: Inspecting or analyzing data to answer a question; collecting data alone is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit analytical knowledge or inspecting/comparing/interpreting data to answer a stated question.
skills.not_sufficient: Collecting, storing, or displaying data without an analytical purpose/action.

skills.definition: Analyzing business/product metrics, defining metrics, or business intelligence.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit business/product analytics knowledge or defining/interpreting business metrics and decision-relevant analyses.
skills.not_sufficient: A business job title, project management, or unexplained numerical results.

skills.definition: Eliciting, analyzing, or translating stakeholder/problem requirements; merely following instructions is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit requirements knowledge or eliciting, clarifying, translating, or negotiating a stakeholder/problem requirement.
skills.not_sufficient: Merely receiving instructions, attending meetings, or completing assigned work.

skills.definition: Statistical methods or knowledge; a tool, degree, or unexplained percentage alone is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit statistical knowledge or applying/interpreting a statistical method.
skills.not_sufficient: A degree, tool name, chart, or unexplained percentage alone.

skills.skill_name: 实验设计与 A/B 测试
skills.definition: Experimental design or conducting A/B/comparative experiments with an explicit setup.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit experimental knowledge or describing experimental setup, comparison groups, assignment, measures, or evaluation.
skills.not_sufficient: Ordinary trial-and-error development or observing before/after numbers without an experimental setup.

skills.definition: Explicit causal inference or methods for estimating causal effects; correlation alone is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit causal-method knowledge or estimating/arguing causal effects using a stated identification approach.
skills.not_sufficient: Correlation, prediction, or saying a result caused improvement without a causal method.

skills.definition: Building or operating repeatable data ingestion, ETL, or transformation pipelines.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit pipeline knowledge or building/operating repeatable ingestion, transformation, or ETL flows.
skills.not_sufficient: A one-off manual download or isolated data edit.

skills.definition: Designing data schemas, entities/relationships, analytical models, or dimensional structures; merely outputting JSON is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit modeling knowledge or defining entities, relationships, schemas, dimensions, or analytical data structures.
skills.not_sufficient: Merely producing JSON, formatting a response, or training a predictive model.

skills.definition: Data cleaning, preparation, validation, quality, or governance practices.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit quality knowledge or cleaning, validating, reconciling, preparing, or governing datasets.
skills.not_sufficient: Data storage, a model-generated assertion of quality, or ordinary UI input checks alone.

skills.definition: Building or maintaining an analytical/business dashboard; a document, handover note, spreadsheet, or isolated chart alone is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit dashboard-building knowledge or personally building/maintaining a dashboard with analytical views, metrics, filters, or refresh behavior.
skills.not_sufficient: A document, handover note, ordinary table, isolated chart, or unspecified reporting alone.

skills.definition: Creating or explicitly designing data visualizations; this does not automatically establish dashboard construction.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit visualization knowledge or designing/creating charts or visual encodings to communicate data.
skills.not_sufficient: A text report or claiming that the team's dashboard existed.

skills.definition: Explicit use or proficiency in BI software; record the actual supported tool.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit proficiency in BI software or using an identified BI platform for a described analytical activity.
skills.not_sufficient: A generic chart, spreadsheet, or database alone; do not infer one BI tool from another.

skills.definition: Data warehouses, warehouse platforms, or warehousing concepts; any ordinary database is not automatically a warehouse.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit warehousing knowledge or designing/querying/operating a warehouse or warehouse-specific analytical structure.
skills.not_sufficient: Any ordinary database or storing files alone.

skills.definition: Processing explicitly large-scale datasets or distributed data workloads; merely naming a framework is insufficient for applied evidence.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit large-scale processing knowledge or described large/distributed workloads, partitioning, resource handling, or scale constraints.
skills.not_sufficient: Merely naming Spark or saying a dataset was big without explicit scale knowledge or work.

skills.definition: Automating or orchestrating analytical/data workflows; a one-off manual analysis is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit workflow-automation knowledge or automating/orchestrating repeated analytical work.
skills.not_sufficient: A single manually executed analysis or unrelated software CI.

skills.definition: Programming in explicitly named non-Python languages. Python is assessed in the separate python core.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit knowledge or personal programming work in a named non-Python language.
skills.not_sufficient: Python-only evidence; Python has its own core.

skills.definition: Python programming or Python-specific development/data libraries; usage does not establish unrelated languages.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit Python knowledge or personally implementing Python logic or using Python libraries for a stated task.
skills.not_sufficient: An AI tool's implementation language or a teammate's Python code.

skills.definition: Software implementation, code quality, testing, debugging, or API engineering in a concrete software context.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit engineering knowledge or personal software implementation, testing, debugging, maintainability, or API work.
skills.not_sufficient: Only using a finished AI product or claiming a team built software.

skills.definition: SQL queries or relational database work; structured JSON alone is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit SQL/relational knowledge or querying, designing, or accessing relational data.
skills.not_sufficient: Structured JSON or generic data storage alone.

skills.definition: Machine-learning concepts, methods, or frameworks; merely calling an AI product is insufficient for applied ML development.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit ML-method/framework knowledge or applying ML methods in a described modeling activity.
skills.not_sufficient: Calling a finished AI API without ML-specific knowledge or development.

skills.definition: Neural/deep-learning methods or models, explicitly stated.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit neural/deep-learning knowledge or working with a described neural architecture/training/inference task.
skills.not_sufficient: Unspecified AI use or ordinary statistical modeling alone.

skills.definition: Mathematical, probability, or statistical foundations; a degree or unexplained numerical result alone is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit mathematical/statistical knowledge or applying a named/clearly described mathematical or statistical method.
skills.not_sufficient: A degree title, numerical output, or unspecified evaluation alone.

skills.definition: Preparing, cleaning, validating, or modeling datasets for analytical/ML use.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit preparation knowledge or cleaning, validating, labeling, structuring, or preparing data for ML/analysis.
skills.not_sufficient: Merely saving model output or invoking inference.

skills.definition: Building or operating repeatable data ingestion, transformation, or processing pipelines.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit pipeline knowledge or building/operating repeatable ingestion, transformation, or processing flows.
skills.not_sufficient: One-off file loading or a standalone inference call.

skills.definition: Creating, selecting, or transforming model input features; merely formatting model outputs is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit feature-engineering knowledge or creating/selecting/transforming inputs used by a model.
skills.not_sufficient: Formatting output JSON or describing a product feature.

skills.definition: Actually training a model; inference or API calls alone are insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit training knowledge or fitting/updating model parameters in a described training process.
skills.not_sufficient: Prompt editing, inference, model selection, or API integration alone.

skills.definition: Explicit fine-tuning/adaptation of a pretrained model; training from scratch or prompt editing alone is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit fine-tuning knowledge or adapting pretrained model weights with a stated process/data.
skills.not_sufficient: Training from scratch, prompt edits, or RAG configuration alone.

skills.definition: Evaluating model quality/performance using a stated evaluation approach; successful execution alone is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit evaluation knowledge or evaluating model behavior using stated data, criteria, metrics, or error analysis.
skills.not_sufficient: Successful execution, outputting a score, or software unit tests unrelated to model quality.

skills.definition: Designing or running controlled/comparative experiments; ordinary iterative implementation alone is insufficient.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit experimental knowledge or designing/running a stated comparison, ablation, controlled test, or experiment.
skills.not_sufficient: Ordinary implementation iterations with no described experimental setup.

skills.definition: Making model inference available through a runnable serving interface and configuring, launching or operating its serving path; local serving can qualify.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit model-serving knowledge, or personally implementing/configuring/launching/operating a stated inference-serving runtime or endpoint.
skills.not_sufficient: Answer-generation behavior, a prototype label, an API framework name, a notebook or a hosted-model request alone, without an actual serving path. Production/cloud scale is not required.
skills.practice_target: An explicitly running/deployed inference service or runnable serving interface with a stated model-inference path.
skills.practice_action: The applicant implements, configures, launches or operates that serving path; calling somebody else's model API alone does not establish deployment.

skills.definition: ML lifecycle operations, such as model versioning, reproducible ML pipelines, monitoring, or continuous model delivery.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit lifecycle-operations knowledge or model versioning, reproducible ML workflows, monitoring, or continuous model delivery.
skills.not_sufficient: An isolated training run or ordinary non-ML CI alone.

skills.definition: Cloud, distributed, container, or operational infrastructure used for AI workloads.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit AI-infrastructure knowledge or personally configuring/operating cloud, compute, distributed, container, or operational infrastructure for AI.
skills.not_sufficient: Calling a cloud AI API without infrastructure work.

modules.module_name: 生成式 AI 与 LLM 应用

skills.definition: Explicit generative-AI knowledge or use; record the actual modality/activity without inferring coding assistance or model training.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit generative-AI knowledge or using/building a system that generates text, images, audio, or other content.
skills.not_sufficient: Generic classification or inferring coding assistance from image-generation work.

skills.definition: Explicit large-language-model knowledge or use; this alone does not establish training, RAG, or agent orchestration.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit LLM knowledge or personal use/development involving a language model.
skills.not_sufficient: Unspecified AI/ML work or assuming every generative model is an LLM.

skills.definition: Retrieval of external context followed by grounded generation; embeddings alone do not establish RAG.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit RAG knowledge or describing retrieval of external context used to ground generated answers.
skills.not_sufficient: Embeddings, a vector database, keyword search, or an LLM alone without retrieval-to-generation linkage.

skills.definition: Model-mediated assistant/agent systems with tool invocation or action orchestration and explicit control flow; bounded single-tool systems qualify.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit agent-system knowledge, or personally designing/implementing a model-mediated tool/action workflow with described invocation, result handling or control logic.
skills.not_sufficient: An agent project name, a plain generation request, fixed search alone or personal decision-making. Autonomy, multiple tools and AI-assisted coding are not prerequisites; denying one does not deny building an agent.
skills.practice_target: A model-mediated tool/action workflow with described invocation, result handling or control flow, including bounded or human-reviewed execution.
skills.practice_action: The applicant personally designs or implements that workflow; neither broad autonomy nor multiple tools are required.

skills.definition: Explicit design, refinement, or evaluation of prompts; a casual model query alone is insufficient for applied evidence.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit prompt-design knowledge or deliberately designing/refining/evaluating prompts for a defined behavior.
skills.not_sufficient: A casual model question or claiming the model followed a prompt.

skills.definition: Embeddings, vector search, or vector storage/retrieval; this alone does not establish a complete RAG pipeline.
skills.direct_evidence: Explicit embedding/vector-search knowledge or using embeddings, similarity search, vector indexing, or vector storage for a stated task.
skills.not_sufficient: Generic arrays, a relational database, or LLM use alone.
